about: Hand-picked, well-documented US events (2001-2025) to label spikes on the charts. A spike that lines up with an event is 'consistent with' it; the app never says the event caused a trend. Dates are the event's main days; precision 'month' means only the month is sure. Research: reports/Climatch monthly trends and redesign.md (Q3).

events.title: Canadian wildfire smoke over Wisconsin
events.summary: Smoke from Canadian wildfires gave Milwaukee its first 'very unhealthy' air-quality day on record (27 June 2023); Wisconsin issued nine smoke advisories that spring and summer.

events.title: Canadian wildfire smoke over New York
events.summary: On 7 June 2023 New York City's daily PM2.5 averaged about 117 µg/m³, its worst air in decades.

events.title: Canadian wildfire smoke returns to Wisconsin
events.summary: Canadian wildfire smoke brought repeated air-quality alerts to Wisconsin in summer 2025.

source.name: Wisconsin Public Radio via Urban Milwaukee, 11 Aug 2025

events.title: West Coast wildfire smoke
events.summary: On 13 September 2020 Portland's air-quality index hit a record 477; the previous record was 157.

events.title: Pacific Northwest heat dome
events.summary: Temperature records were broken by several degrees; the study estimates it was about a 1-in-1000-year event in today's climate.

source.name: Philip et al. 2022, Earth System Dynamics

events.title: Texas freeze (Winter Storm Uri)
events.summary: At least 3,088 daily low-temperature records were tied or broken from 12 to 17 February 2021.

source.name: NOAA Weather Prediction Center event review

events.title: March 2012 heat wave
events.summary: The warmest March on record for the Midwest; Chicago tied or broke its daily record high nine days in a row (14-22 March).

events.title: 2012 Plains and Midwest drought
events.summary: May-August 2012 rainfall deficits over the central Great Plains were the most severe since 1895.

events.title: 2011 Texas drought
events.summary: 2011 was Texas's driest calendar year on record (14.89 in) with its driest summer on record.

events.title: Western drought
events.summary: January-March 2022 was the driest start to a year on record for California and Nevada.

events.title: Hurricane Harvey rain
events.summary: Harvey dropped up to 60.58 in of rain near Nederland, Texas, the US record for a tropical cyclone.

source.name: NOAA National Hurricane Center report AL092017

events.title: Hurricane Helene rain
events.summary: Helene's rain reached 30.78 in at Busick, North Carolina, causing catastrophic flooding around Asheville.

source.name: NOAA National Hurricane Center report AL092024

events.title: Hurricane Katrina
events.summary: Katrina made landfall in Louisiana and Mississippi on 29 August 2005 with 8-10+ in of rain over large areas.

source.name: NOAA National Hurricane Center report AL122005

events.title: Camp Fire (Paradise, California)
events.summary: The fire burned about 70,000 acres in its first day and its smoke filled the Sacramento and San Francisco areas.

events.title: Los Angeles fires (Palisades and Eaton)
events.summary: The Palisades (23,448 acres) and Eaton (14,021 acres) fires destroyed over 16,000 structures.
